title: Corsican Republic
capsule: The Corsican Republic was proclaimed in July 1755 under General Pasquale Paoli, who broke with Genoese sovereignty and drafted a constitution — the first written in Italian — that included provisions for popular sovereignty and briefly female suffrage, inspiring republican thinkers across Europe and America. Paoli established a university at Corte in 1765 and minted coinage bearing the Moor's Head, operating a functioning state on the island. Genoa, unable to reassert control, sold its claim to France by the Treaty of Versailles (May 1768); French forces invaded and defeated Paoli's army at the Battle of Ponte Novu in May 1769, ending the republic after fourteen years. Corsica became a French province in 1770, and Paoli went into exile in Britain; notably, Napoleon Bonaparte was born on the island the same year it fell.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The republic's territorial extent — essentially all of Corsica — is well-documented; the dataset's from/to dates of 1757 and 1769 reflect later full administrative consolidation rather than the 1755 proclamation date.
